findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil, for example when a user receives a notification for a topic they never interacted with (watched category, mailing list, invited PM). The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 instead of an unsubscribe. The action should create the row, e.g. via `TopicUser.change`, or handle nil explicitly.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is a non-idempotent toggle on a GET link
findings.body: The action flips the level: anything above regular becomes regular, anything else becomes muted. Clicking the link once on a watched/tracking topic moves it to regular, and a second click mutes it. The route is a GET reachable from emails, and mail clients and link scanners prefetch GET URLs, so merely opening the email can toggle state. The action should set muted deterministically (and a GET should not mutate state at all, ideally a confirm page or POST).

findings.title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
findings.body: `tu.save!` skips `TopicUser.change`, which sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` and publishes `notification_level_change` on MessageBus. As a result the open browser tab for this topic does not update its notification state, and the reason/timestamp are stale. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` instead.

findings.title: track_visit! assigns the topic id to user_id when a raw id is passed
findings.body: `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` uses `topic` in the else branch where `user` was meant. Callers pass a plain integer user id (`TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id` in topics_controller), so `user_id` becomes the topic id. The visit is recorded against the wrong user, and a new TopicUser row is created with `user_id` equal to the topic id. The diff touches this line, so it should be fixed here.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url, which callers may not pass
findings.body: `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` (added in server.en.yml). Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument while building the email, so the email send fails. The option should default to something sensible or the builder should guard against the missing key.

findings.title: List-Unsubscribe header still points at preferences, not the per-topic link
findings.body: The per-topic unsubscribe URL is added to the body, but the `List-Unsubscribe` header in `header_args` still points to `user_preferences_url`. Mail clients' one-click unsubscribe therefore does not offer the per-topic action, which is the feature this PR adds, and the header and body now disagree about what unsubscribing means.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe behaviour
findings.body: The only change is adding an `unsubscribe_url` argument to a spec fixture. Nothing tests `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, the `TopicsController#unsubscribe` toggle/redirect logic, the missing-TopicUser case, or that the rendered body contains the topic unsubscribe link. The controller action, which mutates notification state, has no request spec.

findings.title: PR description is placeholder text
findings.body: The description reads only 'Test 2', so reviewers get no summary of the new per-topic unsubscribe behaviour, the toggle semantics, or the unrelated refactors bundled in (routes reorder, topic-from-params rewrite, TopicUser formatting).
